text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Foreign investments in Poland will reach four billion U.S. dollars this year, Poland's foreign investment agency (PAIZ) director Waldemar Dabrowski said.
- 1996 will be another good year for Poland's economy, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) Warsaw representative Markus Rodlauer said.
- The recently formed Handel 2000 retail chain will introduce telephone shopping services and customer credit cards, the company said.

- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) will buy 5.6 million shares worth $12.68 million in the Zywiec-based Srubena screws manufacturer after approval by the shareholders' general meeting, Srubena president Bogumil Banas said.

- Poland's Bank Handlowy (BH) will be privatised through sales of two 30 percent stakes - one in a public offer and the other to foreign institutional investors. A five percent stake will be offered to the bank's employees on preferential terms, a senior finance ministry official said.
- IBCA rating agency has awarded Bank Slaski's longterm securities a BBB while its short-term securities received an A3 rating.
NOWA EUROPA
- Poland's economic growth will receive a boost in November thanks to high domestic consumption and foreign investments, the Nicom Consulting Ltd said.
- An electric power surplus in Poland's energy sector creates favourable conditions for competitive offers by the industry, national power grid (PSE) president Zdzislaw Bicki said.

- By the year-end the listed Lubawa technical clothing maker will have sold tents worth 64,000 zlotys to the British army. In future, the company hopes to get exclusive rights for military tent and cover material deliveries for Britain.
- The Krakow-based Strzelec brewery plans to sell up to 7.5 million shares on the Warsaw bourse parallel market following listing next year, the company president Adam Brodowski said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Gillette Poland distribution centre came into operation in Lodz, central Poland, yesterday.

- The Gdansk-based Herbapol herbs maker has recently been privatised, and capital injections from a sister Herbapol company in Lublin saved it from bankruptcy, the Gdansk province privatisation department director Jacek Skarbek said.
- Kings Cross Shopping and the European Trade Centre supermarkets will open in east Warsaw this week. The two centres cost a total of $50 million to build.
ZYCIE
- Sweden's Akerlung Rausing Group has invested $8 million in the Bialystok-based Pakpol packaging maker this year, Pakpol's director Wieslaw Plonka said.
PARKIET
- The listed Ariel shoemaker has bought poliurethane injection equipment worth 505 million lire and a shoe model form for 99 million lire, the company said.
- LG Investment Holdings BV now holds 11.28 million shares in the Lodz-based Petrobank which gives it a controlling stake of more than 50 percent in the bank.
- CS First Boston brokerage house analysts upheld their recommendation to sell the FM Forte furniture maker's shares in a report dated November 4. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
